headline: Iran opens the door to talks: WTI crashes 7% below $97, gold rebounds and long yields slip
summary: Iran's supreme leader cleared the government to negotiate and Trump said he wanted talks to play out, so WTI fell 7.4% to $96.46 and RBOB 8.1% to $2.90, the biggest drops since April. Cheaper oil eased hike fears just enough for gold to bounce 1.8% to near $3,945 and silver about 3% back above $50, while a strong ISM kept the 2-year flat and the 10-year fell about 3bp to near 4.90%. Bunds were steady as euro PMI input costs jumped, and French OATs rallied about 4bp, shrugging off Fitch's negative outlook.
drivers: Iran diplomacy deflates the oil premium

IRNA said Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei authorised the government to pursue talks, after reports that Trump told Netanyahu to let negotiations run. WTI settled -$7.66 at $96.46 and Jan Brent -$8.66 at $104.77, both down over 7%, as CTAs cut Brent longs; OPEC+ held December targets on Sunday.
Oil relief helps metals and long bonds

Lower crude trimmed inflation worries and the dollar index eased to near 101.9, so Comex gold settled +$71.20 at $3,956.90, its best day since September, and the 10-year fell about 3bp. Markets still price a December Fed hike but less tightening into mid-2027.
Strong factories keep the front end pinned

October ISM manufacturing rose to 55.5 vs 54.5 expected with production at 59.0, though prices paid eased to 75.2; September construction spending fell 1.9%. The 2-year held near 4.59% while AI and chip selling dragged the Nasdaq down about 1%.

The final euro-area manufacturing PMI was 52.7 with input costs near four-year highs, adding to ECB hike pressure, so Bunds were flat to slightly weaker at the front. French 10-year yields fell about 4bp to near 4.93% despite Fitch's negative outlook, narrowing the spread to Bunds.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled down $7.66 (-7.4%) at $96.46, the biggest drop in three months; Jan Brent -7.6% at $104.77.
oil.why: Crude's war premium unwound fast after Iran's state media said the supreme leader approved government talks and Iran–Qatar talks continued, following reports that Trump wants diplomacy to play out before any strike. WTI broke $100 in the European morning and hit $95.15, with trend-following funds cutting Brent longs from 100% to about 91%. OPEC+ kept December targets unchanged on Sunday, a non-event.
oil.outlook: Bias lower but volatile in a $93–103 range while talks hold; the Oct 20 low near $95 and the $93.25–95.50 zone are key support. Fresh tanker attacks in Hormuz or a post-midterm strike would quickly send WTI back above $103.
oil.watch: The midterms Nov 3, EIA stocks Nov 4 and any US–Iran deal or Hormuz incident.

gas.note: Dec RBOB fell 25.64¢ (-8.1%) to $2.9001, the lowest settle since Aug 5; AAA pump average near $4.16, down 12¢ in a week.
gas.why: Gasoline fell even harder than crude as the Iran talks removed the Gulf supply premium that last week's Saudi refinery headlines had added, on the first day with December in front. Fundamentals were already soft: EIA showed a 3.9 million barrel build last week, refinery maintenance is ending and driving demand is fading with cooler weather. GasBuddy sees the national average under $4 within a week.
gas.outlook: Range $2.80–3.05 with a downside bias as seasonal demand fades and crude loses its premium. A collapse in the Iran talks or confirmed Gulf refinery damage would put $3.05 back in play.
gas.watch: EIA stocks Nov 4, refinery restarts and US–Iran headlines.

gold.note: Spot rose about $68 (+1.8%) to near $3,945; Comex Nov settled +$71.20 at $3,956.90, its best day since Sept 3.
gold.why: Gold bounced from Friday's one-year low as the 7% oil slump eased inflation fears that had pushed December hike odds up, and the dollar and long yields both slipped. Short covering and bargain buying added after the 14-day RSI fell below 30 last week. A strong 55.5 ISM and still-priced December hike capped the bounce below $3,970.
gold.outlook: Bias for a choppy recovery in a $3,850–4,020 range. A daily close back above $4,000 would confirm a washout low; a hot payrolls on Nov 6 locking in a December hike would push it back to $3,850.
gold.watch: The midterms Nov 3, the refunding and ISM services Nov 4 and payrolls Nov 6.

silver.note: Spot rose about 3% to near $50.70, back above $50 after Friday's break; it gained more than gold.
silver.why: Silver rebounded harder than gold as its higher-beta profile works both ways: lower oil and softer yields eased the macro pressure and shorts covered after last week's 9% drop. A solid ISM, with production at 59.0, also helped the industrial side. Renewed selling in chip stocks kept gains in check, and the gold/silver ratio eased to about 78.
silver.outlook: Range $48–53 with a fragile recovery bias. Holding $50 and clearing $52 would show the liquidation is done; another tech slide or a hot payrolls could send it back toward $48.
silver.watch: ISM services Nov 4, China trade data and payrolls Nov 6.

us2y.note: Little changed near 4.59%; December hike pricing held up despite oil's slump.
us2y.why: The 2-year ignored oil's 7% drop because the data argued against easing hike bets: October ISM manufacturing rose to 55.5 vs 54.5 expected, with production up to 59.0, and prices paid remained elevated at 75.2 even after easing. A 1.9% drop in September construction spending was the offset. Markets still price a December hike but trimmed tightening further out.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.50–4.70%. A strong payrolls on Nov 6 or an oil rebound would pull it toward 4.70%; a weak jobs report or a deeper equity selloff could test 4.50%.
us2y.watch: JOLTS Nov 3, ADP and ISM services Nov 4 and payrolls Nov 6.

us5y.note: Down about 3bp to near 4.70%, the curve's belly following oil lower.
us5y.why: The 5-year rallied as the oil crash lowered expected inflation over the next few years, which matters most for the belly, and AI-stock selling kept haven demand in place. The strong ISM stopped the move short, since it supports the Fed's case for one more hike, so the curve steepened slightly from the 2-year.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.62–4.80%. Successful Iran talks and soft jobs data would favour 4.62%; a hot payrolls or oil back above $103 would lift it toward 4.80%.
us5y.watch: The Nov 4 refunding, ISM services and payrolls Nov 6.

us10y.note: Down about 3bp to near 4.90%, a third straight decline and the lowest since early September.
us10y.why: Cheaper oil was the main driver: WTI's $7.66 drop cut inflation compensation, and renewed selling in chip and AI stocks such as Marvell, Intel and AMD kept money flowing into Treasuries. September construction spending fell 1.9% against a 0.3% gain expected. The ISM beat limited the rally, and investors held back before the midterms and Wednesday's refunding.
us10y.outlook: Range 4.82–4.98%. Quiet midterms and more long-end buybacks at the refunding could test 4.82%; a hot payrolls or a renewed oil spike would bring 5% back into view.
us10y.watch: The midterms Nov 3, the refunding Nov 4 and payrolls Nov 6.

us30y.note: Down about 3bp to near 5.28%, in line with the 10-year.
us30y.why: The long bond rallied with the 10-year as lower oil eased long-run inflation fears. Positioning before Wednesday's refunding also helped: dealers expect unchanged coupon sizes, and markets are watching for less long-end issuance or bigger buybacks, which would support the 30-year. Heavy tech bond supply and term premium limited the move.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.18–5.38%. Guidance for more buybacks would favour 5.18%; larger long-end supply or an oil rebound would push it toward 5.38%.
us30y.watch: The Nov 4 refunding, payrolls Nov 6 and the 30-year auction mid-November.

de2y.note: Up about 2bp to near 3.03–3.05%, as euro PMI cost pressure offset cheaper energy.
de2y.why: The Schatz paused after its October rally. The final euro-area manufacturing PMI was revised up to 52.7 from a 52.4 flash, with input cost inflation near four-year highs, which S&P Global said adds pressure on the ECB to hike again. That outweighed lower oil and gas prices and a surprise 2% drop in German September retail sales.
de2y.outlook: Range 2.95–3.10%. The euro flash CPI on Nov 4 sets direction: a hot print would lift it toward 3.10%, a soft one, helped by lower energy, could test 2.95%.
de2y.watch: Euro flash CPI Nov 4 and ECB speakers.

de5y.note: Up about 1bp to near 3.11%, little changed as costs and cheaper oil offset.
de5y.why: The 5-year was pulled two ways: falling oil and a near-11% intraday drop in European gas prices cut inflation expectations, but strong PMIs, with Germany at 54.2, and surging input costs kept ECB hike bets alive. The ECB also flagged AI valuations and bond-market stress as top stability risks, which did not change rate expectations.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.02–3.20%. Euro CPI on Nov 4 and US payrolls decide the next move; a sustained oil drop favours the lower end.
de5y.watch: Euro flash CPI Nov 4 and US payrolls Nov 6.

de10y.note: Little changed near 3.30–3.32%, holding most of October's 20bp rally.
de10y.why: The 10-year Bund was steady as cheaper energy and lower Treasury yields offset firm euro PMI data and higher input costs. Investors also moved some haven money back into French and Italian bonds, with the Italy–Germany spread near 117bp, so Bunds lagged Treasuries and OATs. Civil unrest spreading to Germany over the weekend had little effect.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.22–3.40%. A soft euro CPI and stable oil would test 3.22%; Brent back above $110 or a hot CPI would lift it toward 3.40%.
de10y.watch: Euro flash CPI Nov 4, the US refunding and the BoE Nov 5.

de30y.note: Up about 1–2bp to near 3.68%, little changed.
de30y.why: The long end barely moved because the day's drivers, energy prices and ECB pricing, mainly affect shorter maturities, while long yields are anchored by heavy euro-area issuance and global term premium. Investors are waiting for the US refunding to see whether the Treasury cuts long-end supply, which would help long bonds worldwide.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.60–3.78%; a long-end selloff around the US refunding is the main upside risk, more buybacks the main downside one.
de30y.watch: The US refunding Nov 4, the BoE Nov 5 and German supply.

fr2y.note: Up a few bp to near 3.70%, following the Schatz on ECB hike pricing.
fr2y.why: Short OATs tracked ECB pricing rather than French credit risk, so they rose with the Schatz after euro PMI input costs jumped. France's own manufacturing PMI fell to 49.5 from 50.6, its first contraction in three months, with new orders down the most since mid-2025. That weak growth picture did not help the front end, where inflation at 3.8% keeps the ECB in focus.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.60–3.78%, led by ECB pricing and the Nov 4 euro CPI; budget risk hits longer OATs more than this tenor.
fr2y.watch: Euro flash CPI Nov 4 and the budget vote around Nov 3.

fr5y.note: Little changed near 4.28%, with the spread to Bunds slightly tighter.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT held steady as relief that Fitch kept France at A+, cutting only the outlook, offset higher ECB pricing at the front of the curve. Investors had sold French debt heavily last week on weak GDP and 3.8% inflation, so positioning was already short, which limited any negative reaction to the outlook change.
fr5y.outlook: Bias for a stable to slightly tighter spread to Bunds if the budget vote passes; outright direction follows euro CPI and the ECB.
fr5y.watch: The budget vote around Nov 3, euro CPI Nov 4 and the Nov 5 OAT auction.

fr10y.note: Down about 4bp to near 4.93%; the spread to Bunds narrowed about 3–4bp to near 162bp.
fr10y.why: French bonds rallied despite Fitch moving France's A+ rating to a negative outlook after Friday's close, because markets had feared an outright downgrade and positioning was heavily short. Cheaper energy, with oil down 7% and European gas near €100/MWh, also helped higher-yielding euro debt, and OATs outperformed Bunds on the day.
fr10y.outlook: Spread range 155–172bp. Budget progress could narrow it to 155bp and keep the 10-year below 5%; a failed vote or political crisis would send it back toward 172bp and above 5%.
fr10y.watch: The budget vote around Nov 3, the Nov 5 auction and strike, and S&P Nov 27.

fr30y.note: Slightly lower near 5.44%; the long-end spread to Germany is still near 175bp.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT edged lower with the rest of the French curve as relief that Fitch did not downgrade and cheaper oil outweighed fiscal worries. It gained less than the 10-year because the long end carries most of France's debt risk premium, with a long-term auction and a national strike both due on Nov 5.
fr30y.outlook: Range 5.35–5.55% with an upside bias into the Nov 5 auction; a smooth budget vote would ease it toward 5.35%.
fr30y.watch: The budget vote around Nov 3, the Nov 5 auction and strike, and S&P Nov 27.

watch: Next: the US midterms, JOLTS and French budget vote Nov 3, the US refunding, ADP, ISM services, euro flash CPI and EIA stocks Nov 4, the BoE and OAT auction Nov 5, payrolls Nov 6, and OPEC+ Nov 29.
sources: Dow Jones via MarketScreener (US and euro bonds)
